forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Rochford's accounts disclaimed by auditors for four years running; council debt-free and £500k ahead on interest
news_drafts.lead:
Rochford District Council's accounts for 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25 have all been disclaimed by its external auditor, Ernst & Young (EY), meaning the auditor could not fully sign off the accounts (a "disclaimer" is stronger than a qualified opinion). The Audit, Governance and Standards Committee on 5 October has an addendum to the audit plan saying assurance "has not been obtained over the brought-forward balances and some of the movements during the disclaimed periods."

EY's risk assessment says the gaps before 2023/24, particularly in reserves (money the council has put aside) and other cumulative balances, "cannot be sufficiently addressed as part of the 2025/26 audit." It says it will focus on bodies that have shown they can support all planned 2025/26 audit procedures. The council's own paper says progress is behind the expected timescales for rebuilding assurance because the disclaimer period covers three years. The papers say external valuers could not provide suitable supporting evidence for property valuations in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The 2024/25 audit has begun rebuilding assurance, with property, plant and equipment the focus for 2025/26.

The treasury management report (how the council borrows and invests its cash) for the first quarter of 2026/27 is more positive. The council stayed debt-free and took no external borrowing. Interest income is forecast at £1.1m against a £600k budget, which the council attributes to higher opening cash balances after a stronger 2025/26 outturn (the actual figures once the year had ended) and to capital programme slippage that keeps money invested longer. Capital spending, on things that last, is forecast at £11.236m against £11.652m, an underspend of £416k, mainly from the Rochford Town Centre Project. That cuts the planned use of the council's own cash to pay for capital spending (internal borrowing) from £4.4m to £3.984m.

Internal audit's first-quarter update lists four medium-priority recommendations overdue after missing three to five implementation dates, covering overtime, travel and subsistence, policy framework training and debt recovery tools. Management blames "high volume of workload and capacity with the team." Two procurement actions have moved from 4 June to 1 November 2026. Budget-holder analytics are now live.

findings.headline: Pathways capital project (C135) is forecast at £187k against a budget of £115k, a £72k variance.
findings.detail: Pathways has no spend recorded year to date and a forecast £72k above budget. This is the largest overspend in the table. The Director Environment block as a whole is forecast at £1,675k against a £1,632k budget, a £42k variance.
findings.matters: A forecast overspend on one project within a programme that is otherwise forecast below budget shows that variances run in both directions, which matters to finance officers tracking where capital pressures sit.
findings.figures: Budget £115k; year-to-date actual £0k; forecast £187k; variance £72k; Director Environment budget £1,632k, forecast £1,675k, variance £42k

findings.headline: Clements Hall Leisure Centre capital project is forecast at £4,118k against a budget of £4,520k, a £402k variance.
findings.detail: The project shows (£48k) in the year-to-date actual column, which is a negative figure as printed, against a £4,520k budget. The forecast of £4,118k gives a £402k variance. This is the largest project in the programme table by budget.
findings.matters: The largest single project by budget is forecast £402k below its budget, which affects the programme's overall borrowing need and the timing of a leisure asset investment.

findings.headline: Rochford Town Centre capital project (C115) is forecast at £50k against a budget of £500k, a £450k variance.
findings.detail: The C115 Rochford Town Centre line shows nothing spent year to date and a forecast of £50k. This is the largest single project variance in the table. A separate Rochford Town Centre line (C140, £100k budget and forecast) sits under Director Place and shows no variance.
findings.matters: A £450k forecast reduction on one town centre project shows how a single scheme's timing can shift a council's capital position, which matters to other councils running regeneration schemes and to lenders assessing delivery risk.

findings.headline: Rochford's capital programme is forecast at £10,788k against a current budget of £11,794k, £1,005k below budget.
findings.detail: The programme total shows £616k spent year to date against the £11,794k budget. The end-of-year forecast is £10,788k, with a variance of (£1,005k). Most of the variance sits in the Director Assets & Investments block, forecast at £8,189k against £9,236k.
findings.matters: A forecast below budget on a £11.8m programme changes the borrowing need and timing for the year, which matters to finance directors planning their own programmes and to lenders sizing the council's capital financing requirement.
findings.figures: Budget £11,794k; year-to-date actual £616k; forecast £10,788k; variance £(1,005)k; Director Assets & Investments budget £9,236k, forecast £8,189k, variance £(1,047)k

findings.headline: Recycling collection is forecast to overspend by £110k because of a forecast increase in the Norse contract
findings.detail: The paper attributes the Environment & Climate Change overspend of £95k to recycling collection, driven by a forecast increase in the Norse contract, with smaller variances totalling an underspend of £15k offsetting part of it.
findings.matters: A contract cost increase on a outsourced collection service is a specific pressure that other councils with similar delivery arrangements may recognise.
findings.figures: Recycling collection overspend £110k; Environment & Climate Change overspend £95k; smaller variances underspend £15k
findings.quote: Recycling collection is forecasting an overspend of £110k attributable to a forecast increase in the Norse contract.
